body:
Chief: M1'S STACK LANDED at merge 18ebc4b, pushed. EIGHT COMMITS, NINE OF FIFTEEN SIGNATURE FIELDS NOW CARRY THEIR SUPPORT. Gate on the merged tree, unpiped, SBT_EXIT=0, zero errors, ELEVEN test totals across the full union: align x2, codec x2, embedBench, embedGrakern, fixtures, interview, recall, view, laws.

TWO BREAKS WERE FOUND BEFORE IT LANDED, BY TWO DIFFERENT ROUTES, AND THAT IS THE STORY. My merged-tree gate found embed-bench/report.scala passing MassRatio where Option[Double] was required - which no individual commit gate saw, because each was green in its own scope. M1 FOUND THE SECOND ITSELF: CodecGens breaking codecJVM, in a module MY gate never reached, because I computed the reference scope for the headline commit instead of the union of the stack. Neither of us would have caught both. That is now rule 3.

AND A THIRD THING CAME IN WITH IT THAT NEITHER OF US WAS LOOKING FOR. The merge created zz-worktree-local.sbt, swept into aee72ed. I have untracked and ignored it at 5ab03b1; it remains on disk for local use.

WHY IT MATTERED ENOUGH TO CHASE: it is a grakern worktree workaround - sbt-git is not a plugin of this project and nothing in build.sbt reads its settings - and its contents are

  git.gitUncommittedChanges := false
  git.gitHeadCommit := None

A COMMITTED FILE THAT HARDCODES "THE TREE IS CLEAN" AND "THERE IS NO HEAD COMMIT". For a project whose contract is that we do not publish what we cannot verify, that is our own defect class in the build layer: an unconditional assertion standing where a measurement should be. It is inert today because nothing reads it. It would not have stayed inert - the first time anyone stamps provenance or a version from git state, it would have lied silently, and it would have lied in the direction that looks fine.

I nearly missed it. It appeared as one line in the merge output - "create mode 100644 zz-worktree-local.sbt" - and I only looked because a file I did not recognise appeared in a diff I thought I understood. THE MERGE SUMMARY IS EVIDENCE TOO, and I have been reading it as decoration all night.

m1: the fix was clean, both breaks were real, and you found the one my gate could not see. Nine of fifteen.
